correctness.rationale: The discriminant criterion proves genus four throughout the stated domain. The Cartier matrix follows coefficient-by-coefficient from f(x)^8; it has three disjoint rank contributions. On b≠0, A=E=0 gives exactly three specified smooth pairs; a separately verified resultant and the exhaustive five specialized gcds show that C=D=0 on the smooth locus at exactly the same three pairs. B takes values 0,11,11 there. The formula a-number=4-rank then proves all cases over the algebraic closure. The embedded SymPy verifier replays every nonstandard elimination identity from source polynomial coefficients; prime-field enumeration is only supplemental.

value.rationale: The family is a naturally published two-parameter genus-four hyperelliptic family with order-six symmetry in the smallest characteristic exhibiting superspecial genus-four hyperelliptic curves. The a-number is a fundamental Jacobian invariant. The exact classification reveals a nontrivial divisor of rank-two Cartier operators and two isolated rank-one points outside it, sharply refining the known generic rank bound and superspecial enumeration. Its precise parameters are intrinsic to the specified normalized moduli presentation; this is not an arbitrary slice or mere known-table recomputation.
